A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExoPredicator work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching material across layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments in five simulated robotics environments, including success rates and learning curves in Figure 6, learned models in Appendix C.1, and planning statistics in Appendix C.2.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results and additionally reports learning-time observations in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The predicate-invention procedure, LLM-guided Bayesian process learning, variational parameter estimation, and planner are retained. Revised notation and newly specified distribution and initialization details document the existing approach without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Coffee, Grow, Boil, Domino, and Fan with the same task requirements and generalization scenarios, including impossible Domino tasks. Section 6 and Appendix B introduce no additional domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains Manual, MAPLE, both ViLA variants, VisPred, and the same ablations. The Appendix C.2 planning table retains Manual, Ours, and No invent. The added runtime discussion concerns existing HRL and VLM baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 extends resource evaluation to wall-clock learning time per online iteration and an illustrative token-cost calculation. The existing task splits, 50 held-out tests, demonstration counts, rollout budgets, and success metrics remain unchanged. Newly disclosed hardware and distribution settings do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a limited computational-efficiency analysis covering learning time, HRL runtime growth, and illustrative LLM costs. The No Bayes, No LLM, Manual-d, and No invent ablations, learned-process examples, and Boil failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Section 6 changes the stated averaging from three to five random seeds. Figure 6 newly identifies its existing error bars and shaded regions as ±1 standard deviation. The unchanged plot images do not establish whether additional runs occurred or plotted statistics were recalculated.

E6.justification: Figure 6, the learned-process examples, and the existing success/planning-time table remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 newly reports 30–360 seconds per ExoPredicator learning iteration, approximately 600 seconds on average for HRL with cases reaching 3200 seconds, and an illustrative $0.0225 token cost. These are additional resource findings, not improved task performance.

T1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.3 retain the causal-process semantics, planning heuristic, and probabilistic-model/ELBO derivations. The shorter main-text ELBO display summarizes retained mathematics; the indicator explanations restate existing activation and persistence semantics. No new proof or substantive theoretical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learning symbolic abstractions and delayed endogenous/exogenous processes from limited data, enabling efficient planning and generalization across five simulated domains.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly explains that the modeled exogenous processes are task-relevant and can be causally downstream of agent actions, distinguishing them from other uses of 'exogenous.' Appendix C.2 adds explanations of growing HRL learning costs and recurring VLM planning costs. Existing Boil failure and simplified-perception limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 and C.3 disclose uniform categorical initialization, absence of clustering hyperparameters, discrete Gaussian delays supported on 1–300, and log-parameter initialization with mean 0 and standard deviation 0.01. Appendix C.2 adds hardware and cost details. Conversely, v1's code-release footnote is removed; this does not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 adds Efroni et al. (2021) and Garrett et al. (2021), qualifies the introduction's PDDL comparison, and softens the characterization of earlier predicate-learning methods. It adds a more complementary account of HRL that acknowledges implicit exogenous dynamics, although the older HRL paragraph remains.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory expansions, clearer raw-versus-abstract trajectory notation, a bulleted search explanation, and a new Appendix C.3. The overall organization remains stable. The publication header changes, and Section 7 acquires a duplicated HRL discussion.

P2.justification: All six figures retain their image content. Figure 6 moves from page 8 to page 9 and gains an uncertainty explanation in its caption. The main-text ELBO display is shortened, and added prose shifts the unchanged Appendix C.2 table downward. No new empirical figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: V3 provides modest gains in clarity and reporting through explicit uncertainty annotation, clearer process explanations, and useful initialization, hardware, and runtime details. These benefits are partly offset by removal of the code pointer and retention of overlapping, differently qualified HRL paragraphs. The unchanged performance displays and unexplained seed-count revision do not establish stronger empirical evidence; the overall gain is limited to documentation and interpretability.
